questions.text: What is a gerund?
opts: A verb ending in -ing used as a noun
questions.correct: A verb ending in -ing used as a noun
questions.hint: "A gerund is simply a verb that ends in -ing and functions as a noun."

questions.text: What does the infinitive usually represent?
opts: Plans, hopes, and intentions for the future
questions.correct: Plans, hopes, and intentions for the future
questions.hint: "The infinitive often describes something that hasn't happened yet: a plan, an intention, a hope."

questions.text: "I enjoy to swim" is correct English.
questions.hint: "I enjoy to swim is wrong. I enjoy swimming." — enjoy requires gerund.

questions.text: What is the difference between "I stopped smoking" and "I stopped to smoke"?
opts: "Stopped smoking" = quit; "stopped to smoke" = paused to smoke
questions.correct: "Stopped smoking" = quit; "stopped to smoke" = paused to smoke
questions.hint: Gerund after "stopped" = the action that ended. Infinitive = the purpose of pausing.

questions.text: Verbs like enjoy, mind, avoid always take the ___ form.
questions.hint: "Verbs that insist on a gerund: enjoy, mind, avoid, miss, consider..."

questions.text: What is the best approach to learning gerund/infinitive patterns?
questions.hint: "Learning which verbs take which form is largely a question of exposure and practice."

questions.text: What has Rustam decided to stop doing in the evenings?
questions.hint: "I've decided to stop checking my phone in the evenings."

questions.text: What does Rustam enjoy doing before bed instead?
questions.hint: "I've started reading instead. I'd forgotten how much I enjoy reading before bed."

questions.text: Kamila says she never forgets to check her planner.
questions.hint: "I love making lists too, but I tend to forget checking them."

questions.text: What has Rustam promised himself to do three times a week?
questions.hint: "I've promised myself to exercise three times a week."

questions.text: Rustam and Kamila agree to check in with each other every ___ morning.
questions.hint: "Let's agree to check in every Monday morning."

questions.text: Why does Rustam say he has been avoiding change for too long?
opts: He kept putting off making changes — now he refuses to keep drifting
He had no reason to change
questions.correct: He kept putting off making changes — now he refuses to keep drifting
questions.hint: "I've been avoiding making changes for too long. I refuse to keep drifting."

questions.text: "I enjoy ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "enjoy" + GERUND. "I enjoy READING." ✅

questions.text: "She decided ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "decide" + INFINITIVE. "She decided TO GO." ✅

questions.text: "He keeps ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "keep" + GERUND. "He keeps FORGETTING." ✅

questions.text: "She refused ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "refuse" + INFINITIVE. "She refused TO ANSWER." ✅

questions.text: "I look forward to ___ you." (see)
questions.hint: "look forward TO" + GERUND. "TO" = preposition here! "SEEING." ✅

questions.text: "Avoid ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "avoid" + GERUND. "Avoid EATING late." ✅

questions.text: "I stopped ___ means I no longer do it." Which?
questions.hint: "stopped SMOKING" = the action stopped. I no longer smoke. ✅

questions.text: "She asked him ___." Choose.
questions.hint: "ask + object + TO + base". "She asked him TO HELP." ✅

questions.text: "She tends to procrastinate." "Procrastinate" means:
questions.hint: "procrastinate" = to keep delaying something that should be done.

questions.text: "The distinction is not always about time." "Distinction" means:
questions.hint: "distinction" = a clear difference between two things.

questions.text: "Both forms are acceptable." "Acceptable" means:
questions.hint: "acceptable" = allowed; considered good enough.

questions.text: Learning is a question of ___ and practice — contact with the language.
questions.hint: "exposure" = contact with and experience of something regularly.

questions.text: "He clearly stated his intention." "Intention" means:
opts: Plan or aim for the future
questions.correct: Plan or aim for the future
questions.hint: "intention" = a plan or aim; what you intend to do.
